subject: Post-demo: capacity alignment and latency/throughput tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Tran <alyssa@fastlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-02T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: capacity alignment and latency/throughput tradeoffs

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so we can line up the right pilot path: 

1) Workload profile you mentioned: ~600 qps peak for product search, median request ~12 tokens input / 40 tokens output, but 10% of queries are longer (product descriptions ~200 tokens). You flagged p99 latency goal of ~120ms for the search scoring call.

2) Isolation & data controls: you prefer a VPC path if we need strict tenancy or on-prem, but the team wants to start with a hosted pilot to validate latency/cost before escalating to Dedicated or Private.

3) Key technical clarifications we need to size a pilot:
   - Confirm estimated sustained qps and burst factor (you said 600 peak, is sustained 300?).
   - Typical max sequence length distribution (how often do the 200-token cases appear?).
   - Whether caching of product prefix is feasible from your side (would reduce steady cost/latency).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
- We run a 72-hour hosted pilot with continuous observability on token-level latency and cost, and an A/B route to a Dedicated pool if hosted cannot meet p99 120ms.
- We’ll provide a sample trace bundle (attached) and a short SLA spreadsheet so procurement can see the Dedicated commitment tiers.
- Ask from your infra: a small sample of anonymized request traces (or a synthetic qps script) so we can run an internal perf model and provide a recommendation (hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC).

If Hosted meets p99 at your profile with acceptable cost, we can keep you on Hosted API and add a burst Dedicated overlay for peak days. If not, we’ll scope Dedicated capacity (GPU pool size, prewarming) or Private VPC if you require tenant isolation.

Can you confirm sustained qps and whether infra can provide traces by Friday? Once we have those, Karthik and I will size the pilot and share pricing options.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Alyssa Tran <alyssa@fastlane.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: FastLane Infra <infra@fastlane.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-02T18:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: capacity alignment and latency/throughput tradeoffs

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers from our side:

- Sustained qps: ~320 qps during business hours, peaks up to 650 qps during weekend promotions.
- Long-tail requests (~200 tokens) are about 6% of traffic, mostly admin queries and detailed product lookups.
- We can provide a 24-hour anonymized trace slice by EOD Friday and a synthetic load script (JMeter) that matches our peak burst pattern.

Regarding isolation: procurement prefers Dedicated for medium-term commitments, but engineering wants to validate hosted performance first. So your suggested hosted pilot with a Dedicated fallback sounds right.

Two asks for Redwood:
1) Can you indicate the likely Dedicated pool size (rough GPU estimate) for 650 qps with our token distribution? Even a ballpark will help procurement.
2) What’s the expected p99 delta between Hosted (multi-tenant) and a single-tenant Dedicated pool for these models — do you typically see 20–40ms difference after batching/caching?

We’ll get the traces to you and the synthetic script by Friday.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Product Lead — ML Systems
FastLane Retail
alyssa@fastlane.com

Folks — forwarding Alyssa’s replies. Action items I’m proposing for Redwood: 

1) Karthik: please run a quick perf model (estimate GPU count + memory) for 650 qps with 6% long-tail 200-token requests. Use the attached trace sample and assume a conservative 1.2x burst factor. Deliverable: recommended Dedicated pool config and expected p99 for Dedicated versus Hosted. Target EOD Thursday.

2) Marissa: draft a Hosted 72-hour pilot runbook (observability hooks, logging we’ll need, SLA gating criteria). Include the steps to flip traffic to a Dedicated overlay if p99 > 120ms for more than 30 minutes.

3) I’ll prepare pricing bands and the short explanation for procurement on how burst Dedicated overlay pricing works (commit tiers vs burst on-demand).

Also note — procurement will likely want the pilot-sla-sheet.xlsx (attached) and a short note on data retention and auditability for the Hosted pilot (they flagged SOC2 controls). I’ll include standard redwood compliance bullets.

If either of you foresee the need to recommend starting directly on Dedicated or VPC given these numbers, flag that in your outputs — but tentatively we propose Hosted pilot + Dedicated fallback.

Ben
